AROUND TOWN
First Tracks Award
STOWE — Vermont Ski and Snowboard Museum will honor Stowe skier Noah Dines as its 2025 First Tracks Award recipient, Jan. 16, at 1 South Main St., Stowe. Doors open at 5:45 p.m.; the award ceremony begins at 6:30 p.m.
The award recognizes a Vermonter younger than the age of 35 who has “made a significant accomplishment in skiing or snowboarding and has enriched Vermont’s snow sports heritage.”
In 2024, at age 30, Dines set a new world record for the most human-powered vertical feet skied in a single calendar year, accumulating 3,590,097 vertical feet between Jan. 1 and Dec. 30, an effort equivalent to climbing Mount Everest more than 120 times. Beginning and ending his quest in Stowe, Dines surpassed the previous record in early September, reached his personal goal of 3 million vertical feet by late October, and continued skiing through year’s end.
His journey took him across Vermont and around the world, including the Alps, the Pacific Northwest, and South America, as he chased winter conditions and averaged more than 9,800 vertical feet per day.
The award will be presented during a Red Bench Speaker Series program at Vermont Ski and Snowboard Museum. The evening will include the premiere of a short film produced by the Museum in honor of Dines’ accomplishment, followed by a conversation with David Goodman, ski journalist and author.
Admission is $25 and must be purchased in advance. Capacity is limited. Register here: www.vtssm.org/new-events online.
The First Tracks Award, established in 2017, is given in memory of Ian Graddock, a former Vermont Ski and Snowboard Museum board member, lifelong skier and volunteer.
Event sponsors include: The Stowe Group at Morgan Stanley, rk Miles, Spruce Peak Realty, Sisler Builders, Green Mountain Inn, and von Trapp Brewing.
Community members are also invited to nominate future First Tracks Award recipients. Nomination requirements are available on the museum’s website.
History workshops
The Vermont Historical Society has been awarded a grant from the U.S. Department of Education to facilitate professional development workshops for teachers. Aimed at improving access to the Vermont History Day program, workshops will take place in fall in the Northeast Kingdom. Teachers will be able to apply to get a stipend to attend, and applications will open in the fall, date TBD.
This American History and Civics Seminars Program grant will support professional development opportunities held in Colorado, Idaho, Iowa, Ohio, Utah, Vermont, Virginia and Wisconsin. National History Day, in conjunction with its affiliate partners in each state, will co-lead these workshops.
